title_py: Nǐ jiào shénme míngzi? Jǐ suì?
auditory_note: Tap ▶ Listen to play each clip.

banner.body_en: Your three spoken sentences scored 45 out of 45, so your tones out loud are sounding great. Written tone marks are still the main thing costing points, so keep adding them. Lesson 8 (numbers) is still open whenever you're ready.
banner.body_py: Nǐ de sān gè kǒuyǔ jùzi dé le sìshíwǔ fēn, mǎnfēn! Nǐ shuō de shēngdiào hěn hǎo. Xiě pīnyīn de shíhou, hái yào jiā shēngdiào. Dì-bā kè nǐ zhǔnbèi hǎo le jiù huífù.

intro.en: Hi Evan! Yesterday you learned to count to five. Today we'll put those numbers to work with two of the very first questions anyone asks a child (or a new friend): "What's your name?" and "How old are you?" You'll learn jiào (to be called), míngzi (name), shénme (what), and suì (years old). By the end, you'll be able to tell someone your kids' ages in Mandarin. We'll also review hello, thank you, goodbye, friend, and person, since those are overdue.
intro.py: Nǐ hǎo, Evan! Zuótiān nǐ xué le cóng yī shǔ dào wǔ. Jīntiān wǒmen yòng zhèxiē shùzì wèn liǎng gè zuì chángjiàn de wèntí: “Nǐ jiào shénme míngzi?” hé “Nǐ jǐ suì?” Nǐ huì xué jiào, míngzi, shénme hé suì. Xué wán yǐhòu, nǐ jiù kěyǐ yòng Zhōngwén shuō nǐ háizi jǐ suì le. Wǒmen yě fùxí nǐ hǎo, xièxie, zàijiàn, péngyou hé rén.

blocks.note_en: One sharp 4th-tone drop. Wǒ jiào Evan means "I'm called Evan," which is the everyday way to say your name.
blocks.note_py: Dì-sì shēng. Wǒ jiào Evan jiù shì shuō nǐ de míngzi.

blocks.note_en: Rising 2nd tone on MÍNG, then a light, quick neutral zi.
blocks.note_py: Míng shì dì-èr shēng, zi shì qīngshēng.

blocks.note_en: Rising 2nd tone on SHÉN, then a soft neutral me. Like shéi (who), it sits right where the answer would go, not at the front.
blocks.note_py: Shén shì dì-èr shēng, me shì qīngshēng. Gēn shéi yíyàng, shénme fàng zài dá'àn de wèizhi.

blocks.note_en: 4th tone. Put it right after the number, with no shì: Tā sì suì means "He is four."
blocks.note_py: Dì-sì shēng. Fàng zài shùzì hòumiàn, bú yòng shì: Tā sì suì.

blocks.note_en: Word for word: "You are called what name?" The question word shénme simply replaces the answer.
blocks.note_py: Zhè jù huà jiù shì: nǐ jiào shénme míngzi? Shénme tìhuàn dá'àn.

blocks.en: How old is he/she? (for a child)
blocks.note_en: Use jǐ (how many, from Lesson 8) for kids under about ten. To ask "How old are you?" to a child, say Nǐ jǐ suì? and the two 3rd tones change: say it like ní jǐ suì.
blocks.note_py: Wèn xiǎo háizi yòng jǐ. Nǐ jǐ suì? Liǎng gè dì-sān shēng zài yìqǐ, nǐ yào shuō chéng ní.

blocks.title: 🔑 Pattern: question words stay in place
blocks.body_en: In English we move the question word to the front. In Chinese you keep the sentence order and just swap the answer for the question word. The question and the answer look almost the same.
blocks.body_py: Yīngwén bǎ wèncí fàng zài qiánmiàn. Zhōngwén bú biàn yǔxù, zhǐ yòng wèncí tìhuàn dá'àn. Wèntí hé dá'àn chàbuduō yíyàng.

pairs.en: What's your name? / My name is Evan.
pairs.py: Nǐ jiào shénme míngzi? / Wǒ jiào Evan.

pairs.en: How old is he? / He is four.
pairs.py: Tā jǐ suì? / Tā sì suì.

blocks.title: ✨ Bonus: one and a half
blocks.body_en: Half is bàn, and it goes after suì. Notice yī becomes yí before the 4th-tone suì, just like yí gè. Perfect for your youngest!
blocks.body_py: Yí bàn shì bàn, fàng zài suì hòumiàn. Yī zài dì-sì shēng qiánmiàn biànchéng yí, gēn yí gè yíyàng.

pairs.en: She is one and a half.

blocks.en: These five are overdue. Listen, then say each one out loud. Notice how nǐ hǎo becomes ní hǎo when you speak, because two 3rd tones meet.
blocks.py: Zhè wǔ gè cí yào fùxí le. Xiān tīng, ránhòu dàshēng shuō. Nǐ hǎo shuō de shíhou yào biànchéng ní hǎo, yīnwèi liǎng gè dì-sān shēng zài yìqǐ.

blocks.en: My friend is called Xiǎo Míng.
blocks.py: Wǒ de péngyou jiào Xiǎo Míng.

blocks.en: She is one and a half.

practice.how_to: Type your answers in the boxes below. Use tone marks on every pinyin answer (missing tones earn half credit). For 🎤 S1–S3, record a short clip on this page (you can replay and re-record; each clip stops at about 20 seconds). Then tap Submit to see your written score right away.

intro_callout.title: Send a voice memo in Mandarin Tutor chat
intro_callout.body_en: Email can't record audio. Listen to each model first, then read S1–S3 aloud in one memo. Watch the tone changes: ní hǎo in S1, and wǒ yǒu said like wó yǒu in S3.
intro_callout.body_py: Diànzǐ yóujiàn bù néng lùyīn. Xiān tīng, ránhòu bǎ S1 dào S3 dàshēng dú chūlái. S1 lǐ shuō ní hǎo, S3 lǐ wǒ yǒu shuō chéng wó yǒu.

items.prompt_en: I have two kids. He is four.
items.prompt_py: Wǒ yǒu liǎng gè háizi. Tā sì suì.

closing.en: Nice work, Evan! Tonight, try asking your four-year-old "Nǐ jǐ suì?" and see if they'll hold up four fingers. Tap Submit when your written answers and voice memos are ready. Jiāyóu!
closing.py: Zuò de hěn hǎo, Evan! Jīntiān wǎnshang, shìshi wèn nǐ sì suì de háizi: “Nǐ jǐ suì?” Nǐ zhǔnbèi hǎo le jiù huífù, yǔyīn qǐng fā dào Mandarin Tutor liáotiān lǐ. Jiāyóu!
